title: Rectangular base
spec: Start by setting up a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees in all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, create a new face and draw a closed loop using four lines. The first line starts at the origin [0.0, 0.0] and ends at [0.0254, 0.0]. The second line extends from [0.0254, 0.0] to [0.0254, 0.75]. The third line runs from [0.0254, 0.75] to [0.0, 0.75], and the fourth line completes the loop by connecting [0.0, 0.75] back to the origin. After drawing the closed loop, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to reduce its size proportionally. Ensure that the sketch remains aligned with the original coordinate system by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector of zero. Finally, extrude the scaled 2D sketch along the normal direction by 0.0064 units to create a 3D solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular base are 0.02540220152413209 meters in length, 0.75 meters in width, and 0.0063505503810330245 meters in height.

# Define the initial sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.0254, 0).lineTo(0.0254, 0.75).lineTo(0, 0.75).close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.0064)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0254, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0254, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.0064)
